title: Horace Parlan in June Clark's dancing school band
summary: McRae remembers pianist Horace Parlan, with a crippled hand, working with him at a dancing school, though the dating is confusing.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Horace Parlan played with me before he played with any of those guys. He worked with me --
You know where Horace Parlan worked with us at? You wouldn't believe. He worked with me with June Clark back in them days at the dancing school.
He worked with me at 42nd, he worked with me at that 48th Street or 47th Street -- that dancing school upstairs on Broadway. The same school from 42nd Street. When June got --
He must've been a kid then.

Yeah, he was a kid because when June got in -- Remember that show came out, Just A Minute? June had the trumpet -- had a spot on the stage.
Then we moved up to 48th Street -- it's a dancing school there. 49th Street, on the north side of Broadway.
Owned by the same guy that own the dancing school down at 14th Street where we worked.
We worked up there because we were closer to the theater that June was gonna be in -- that Just A Minute show. That was right off Broadway so he could get to the theater. We'd just switch spots.
Well did he have that problem with his hand at that time?
Then. That's why I remember him from, because he had the thing -- he used to play with the -- but he could play. Amazing -- he could play.
June loved it and he was really good. I think he made a record with me. Maybe went on some
